claims.statement: Text and log-jsonl search keep pending fragment, saved probability, split-before flag, selected count, and found state local to each input; records do not group across files and max-count applies per log input.
Without explicit paths the CLI selects piped stdin or the current directory for terminal use; '-' explicitly selects stdin and explicit paths do not add it implicitly.
Text records preserve original UTF-8 line endings and final unterminated lines, while log-jsonl decodes only string text fields and inserts one additional LF between joined records.
Log-jsonl ignores extra metadata fields and rejects non-object, blank, malformed, missing-text or non-string-text records; text and JSONL reject invalid UTF-8 and NUL including decoded JSONL NUL.

Log fragment coordinates are 1-based inclusive physical lines and 0-based half-open received-input byte ranges; JSONL decoded-records text is not a source byte slice and escaped newlines do not change physical coordinates.
The first log record receives a standalone match evaluation and becomes pending regardless of selection relevance.

An eligible boundary uses one logical model request with current_fragment and next_record and four questions: same_event, useful_context, match_next and match_extended; relation prompts exclude shared-topic-only and independent-match-only justification.
Adjacent records join when same_event or useful_context reaches join-threshold, including equality; joining appends text, preserves split-before and replaces saved relevance with match_extended.
On rejected joining the old fragment completes with its saved score, not match_extended, and continuing search reuses match_next for the new pending fragment without a standalone evaluation.
EOF completes any pending log fragment with its saved probability and no extra evaluation; empty input selects nothing.

Grouping validates all four finite numeric probabilities in [0,1] before returning; evaluation failures propagate without treating pending text as EOF output and retries do not commit duplicate appends.

Physical-line and fragment caps both default to 16384 bytes but measure different representations: physical bytes including line endings versus evaluated UTF-8 text including the JSONL joining LF; reader overflow detection reads at most line cap plus one byte.
A single log record exceeding max-fragment-bytes is indivisible and errors before an existing pending fragment is completed.

A combined-size overflow forces a between-record split before semantic grouping: the old fragment completes with saved score and split_after, and if continuing the next receives standalone match and split_before.
Exactly reaching the fragment byte cap does not complete a fragment because overflow is a strict greater-than check performed only on arrival of another record.

Only completed fragments are selected and counted: normal selection is saved probability at least threshold, inversion selects strictly below it, and threshold and join-threshold independently default to 0.5.
Selected normal log output is flushed immediately, JSON output includes located log fields and split flags, while count suppresses bodies and flushes name:selected at EOF or count-limit stopping.

Log files-with-matches stops each input after printing its first completed selection, quiet stops the invocation without output, and positive max-count stops each input after its selected-fragment limit.
Semantic-boundary stopping occurs after the four-question evaluation but before new pending installation; forced-split stopping occurs before the fresh standalone evaluation of the next record.
A pause in live input does not finish pending fragments; timeout defaults to 30 seconds per model evaluation including retries and response reading rather than serving as an input-idle timeout.
Transient model failures may retry a logical evaluation up to four total HTTP attempts within a shared evaluation budget.

Stdin coordinates refer to the received stream, not the producer's full original file; tail-f results need not have full-file line numbers and transformed JSONL names and coordinates belong to the prepared input.
agrind is an external record-preparation boundary: messages must become string text, relevant level metadata must be included in text, and adjacent prepared records are still grouped by jev-grep.

agrind parse wrapping with noconvert preserves numeric-looking strings but strips surrounding whitespace; agrind json can drop invalid JSON and parse without nodrop can drop unmatched lines, losses or transformations the consumer cannot detect.

The consumer exits 0 for selections, 1 for none, 2 for errors and treats broken stdout pipes as clean exit 0; shell pipefail can additionally expose producer errors and early consumer stopping can cause producer SIGPIPE, so pipeline status differs from consumer status.
ast-grep uses independently evaluated code candidates instead of the pending log-grouping lifecycle.

Offline acceptance tests use a controlled local HTTP server to verify four-question requests, saved-score rejection, equality context joins, split flags, completed-selection stopping, retry commit behavior and pre-EOF streaming; reader unit tests verify byte preservation and input validation.
